goal: Make `blit jobs run` and local `jobs log` resolve bare saved-job names and run IDs consistently regardless of current-directory files, while requiring explicit paths for job or log files and preventing saved names from colliding with generated run IDs.
recommended_approach: Classify every jobs target before filesystem lookup using one shared rule—separator-bearing values are paths and bare values belong to the command's identifier namespace—reserve the generated run-ID shape, centralize detailed name-validation errors, and test both name/file shadowing directions.
comparison: The change correctly centralizes path classification, reserves 32-character lowercase hexadecimal names, updates documentation, and adds effective integration coverage. My independent guard passed at head, failed after restoring file-existence-based classification, and passed again after restoring the exact head. The remaining weakness is that the new reserved-name rule is absent from user-facing validation errors.
material_changes: Update every saved-job-name validation error to explain that 32-character lowercase hexadecimal names are reserved for run IDs, preferably by centralizing validation and its diagnostic.

findings.title: Reserved run-ID names are rejected with contradictory guidance
findings.evidence: crates/blit-cli/src/cli.rs:169 — `parse_job_name` rejects a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal name through `valid_job_name`, but its error lists only conditions that such a name satisfies; crates/blit-core/src/job_record.rs:378 repeats the incomplete rule.
findings.predicted_failure: A user supplying such a name through `--save` or `jobs save` is told it must meet rules it already meets, with no indication that the run-ID namespace is reserved or how to correct the name.
findings.better_approach: Have the shared validator return a specific failure reason and reuse it in both Clap parsing and `SavedJobs::path`, explicitly naming the reserved 32-lowercase-hex run-ID shape.
